Dani, Sonnet Good news — I found several working resources on both topics: ## **Travel Advisor Ecosystem (Consortia & Commissions)** The consortium model works this way: vendors pay commissions to the **host agency** (as the "agency of record"), and the host agency then shares commissions with independent travel advisors. This structure lets smaller advisors access higher commission tiers through the host's collective buying power. Key players: **Virtuoso, Ensemble, Travel Leaders Network, Signature** — each negotiates exclusive rates with cruise lines and hotels. Commission splits typically range **70-90%** to established advisors, depending on volume and the host agency model. **Best working resources:** - [Travel Consortia: Full Guide (Altex)](https://www.altexsoft.com/blog

Dani, Sonnet Great question. Here's the structure of the travel advisor ecosystem: --- ## **Host Agencies vs. Consortia** **Host Agencies** are companies that employ or contract with travel advisors. They handle the business infrastructure (E&O insurance, supplier relationships, accounting) so advisors can focus on selling. **Consortia** are networks that member agencies join to gain leverage — pooled buying power, negotiated commissions, perks from suppliers. Most host agencies are *members of* a consortium. --- ## **The Three Tiers (Big Picture)** | Tier | Players | Reach | |------|---------|-------| | **Largest Consortium** | Travel Leaders Network | ~7,000 locations; 100K+ advisors; $17B+ annual sales | | **Upscale Focus** | Virtuoso | Premium market segment; $25–30B ann
